1.2.1.title: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
1.2.1.description: Any audio-only content should also be conveyed in text. Any video content with no audio track should also be described in text, but could also be described with audio.

1.2.2.title: Captions (Prerecorded)
1.2.2.description: The audio in videos should be captioned.

1.2.3.title: Audio description or media alternative (Prerecorded)
1.2.3.description: Actions, descriptions, and other important non-audio content in videos should be described in captions or a separate audio track.

1.2.4.title: Captions (Live)
1.2.4.description: Live videos that include audio should be captioned.

1.2.5.title: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
1.2.5.description: Actions, descriptions, and other important non-audio content in videos should be described in captions or a separate audio track.

1.2.6.title: Sign Language (Prerecorded)
1.2.6.description: All video that is published after video has sign language interpretation.

1.2.7.title: Extended Audio Description (Prerecorded)
1.2.7.description: Video is sometimes paused in order to give enough time for audio descriptions to be conveyed properly.

1.2.8.title: Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
1.2.8.description: A text-based transcription of a video is offered, on top of closed captions and audio description.

1.2.9.title: Audio-only (Live)
1.2.9.description: Live captioning is provided for live audio.

1.3.1.title: Info and Relationships
1.3.1.description: Information or relationships between content that is visual is also conveyed through the code, via HTML or ARIA (for example the for attribute on a form label, or aria-describedby on an input that has hint text).

1.3.2.title: Meaningful Sequence
1.3.2.description: The visual presentation of the content matches what's read out by a screen reader.

1.3.3.title: Sensory Characteristics
1.3.3.description: Nothing is referred to just by its color, size, position, shape, and so on.

1.3.4.title: Orientation
1.3.4.description: Rotating a device from portrait to landscape doesn't stop everything being perfectly readable and usable.

1.3.5.title: Identify Input Purpose
1.3.5.description: The purpose of form fields can be identified by the browser, so that auto-complete suggestions can be offered in a dropdown.

1.3.6.title: Identify Purpose
1.3.6.description:
Landmark regions and personalisation semantics have been used, so people can use browser tools to do things like:
- Remove non-essential content
- Add identifying icons to particular elements on the page

1.4.1.title: Use of Color
1.4.1.description: Color shouldn't be the only thing used to convey meaning.

1.4.2.title: Audio Control
1.4.2.description: Auto playing audio that lasts more than 3 seconds can be turned down or stopped.

1.4.3.title: Contrast (Minimum)
1.4.3.description: Text has a contrast ratio of 4.5 to 1. Large text can be a 3 to 1 ratio if it's over 24px, or bold and over 19px. Usable components like form fields and buttons, and graphics like pie charts and line graphs should have a contrast ratio of 3 to 1.

1.4.4.title: Resize Text
1.4.4.description:
The page is fully responsive. The content adjusts and is readable and usable:
- When the zoom is set to 200% in the browser's settings
- At viewport sizes from 320px and up
- When custom styles are added to increase the spacing of letters, words, lines, and/or paragraphs

1.4.5.title: Images of Text
1.4.5.description: Text is actual text; not images of text.

1.4.6.title: Contrast (Enhanced)
1.4.6.description: Text has a contrast ratio of 7:1 to 1. Large text can be a 4.5 to 1 ratio if it's over 24px, or bold and over 19px.

1.4.7.title: Low or No Background Audio
1.4.7.description: For spoken audio content, any background noise or music is 20 decibels lower than the foreground speech.

1.4.8.title: Visual Presentation
1.4.8.description:
For blocks of text, such as paragraphs:
- Text should never be justified.
- Line-height should be at least 1.5.
- The width should not exceed 80 characters.
- Users should be able to set text and background colors, often through a custom stylesheet.

1.4.9.title: Images of Text (No Exception)
1.4.9.description: Text is actual text; never images of text.

1.4.10.title: Reflow
1.4.10.description:
The page is fully responsive. The content adjusts and is readable and usable:
- When the zoom is set to 200% in the browser's settings
- At viewport sizes from 320px and up
- When custom styles are added to increase the spacing of letters, words, lines, and/or paragraphs

1.4.11.title: Non-text Contrast
1.4.11.description: Text has a contrast ratio of 4.5 to 1. Large text can be a 3 to 1 ratio if it's over 24px, or bold and over 19px. Usable components like form fields and buttons, and graphics like pie charts and line graphs should have a contrast ratio of 3 to 1.

1.4.12.title: Text Spacing
1.4.12.description:
The page is fully responsive. The content adjusts and is readable and usable:
- When the zoom is set to 200% in the browser's settings
- At viewport sizes from 320px and up
- When custom styles are added to increase the spacing of letters, words, lines, and/or paragraphs

1.4.13.title: Content on Hover or Focus
1.4.13.description: Tooltips can be dismissed, usually via the [esc] key, the text in the tooltip can be selected, and they don't time out on their own.

2.1.1.title: Keyboard
2.1.1.description: You can get around using the keyboard alone.

2.1.2.title: No Keyboard Trap
2.1.2.description: There shouldn't be a situation where you enter a modal with the keyboard and can't get back to where you were.

2.1.3.title: Keyboard (No Exception)
2.1.3.description: You can navigate and interact with a page using the keyboard alone.

2.1.4.title: Character Key Shortcuts
2.1.4.description: Keyboard shortcuts should use modifier keys, like [ctrl], [command], or [alt]/[option].

2.2.1.title: Timing Adjustable
2.2.1.description: Time limits should be avoided unless they're able to be extended.

2.2.2.title: Pause, Stop, Hide
2.2.2.description: Automatically moving/animating content that lasts more than 5 seconds should be able to be stopped or hidden.

2.2.3.title: No Timing
2.2.3.description: Unless it's a live broadcast or something else that's happening in real time, there are no time constraints placed on the user.

2.2.4.title: Interruptions
2.2.4.description: Pop-ups, notifications, and other interruptions can be switched off.

2.2.5.title: Re-authenticating
2.2.5.description: If a logged-in session expires mid-way through a task, any data entered after expiry is kept, so that they don't have to re-enter it when they log in again.

2.2.6.title: Timeouts
2.2.6.description: A warning is shown if a logged-in session is about to expire.

2.3.1.title: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
2.3.1.description: Nothing flashes, blinks, or flickers more than three times in one second.

2.3.2.title: Three Flashes
2.3.2.description: Nothing flashes, blinks, or flickers more than three times in one second.

2.3.3.title: Animation from Interactions
2.3.3.description: Animations triggered by interactions like button presses can be turned off.

2.4.1.title: Bypass Blocks
2.4.1.description: ‘Skip links' are available for keyboard users to jump past navigation.

2.4.2.title: Page Titled
2.4.2.description: Each page has a unique <title> that describes what's on that page.

2.4.3.title: Focus Order
2.4.3.description: When a keyboard user tabs through a page, the order goes from top to bottom and left to right, as you would read the page.

2.4.4.title: Link Purpose (In Context)
2.4.4.description:
It is clear where a link will take you from either:
- The link text itself
- The information in the sentence leading up to the link

2.4.5.title: Multiple Ways
2.4.5.description: Header navigation is not the only way to get around a website; there's another way, such as on-page links, a sitemap, or a site-wide search.

2.4.6.title: Headings and Labels
2.4.6.description: Headings are descriptive of the content that they contain, form labels clearly describe what information is required, and buttons inform the user what will happen when they're pressed.

2.4.7.title: Focus Visible
2.4.7.description: There's visible keyboard focus styling to indicate which element you're currently focused on.

2.4.8.title: Location
2.4.8.description: The user is clearly informed where they are in a set of pages.

2.4.9.title: Link Purpose (Link Only)
2.4.9.description: It is clear where a link will take you from the link text alone, without having to read the text around it.

2.4.10.title: Section Headings
2.4.10.description: Headings are used to group distinct sections on a page.

2.4.11.title: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
2.4.11.description: When tabbing to a focusable item, the element should be at least partially visible; not completely covered by a ‘sticky' footer element, for example. This ensures keyboard users can see where the item that currently has focus is.

2.4.12.title: Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)
2.4.12.description: Almost the same as 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum), but the focusable item should be fully visible when it's tabbed to, so that no scrolling is necessary to bring it into view.

2.4.13.title: Focus Appearance
2.4.13.description: The focus indicators for keyboard users are easy to spot: they are at least 2px thick and have a contrast ratio of 3 to 1 (or higher) against their unfocused state.

2.5.1.title: Pointer Gestures
2.5.1.description: All actions that are carried out using a gesture (swiping, pinching, and so on) or drawing, can also be done with a button or buttons.

2.5.2.title: Pointer Cancellation
2.5.2.description: Actions (like pressing a button) aren't triggered on mouse-down; rather on mouse-up.

2.5.3.title: Label in Name
2.5.3.description: The visible text of a form field, button, or link matches the text in the underlying code.

2.5.4.title: Motion Actuation
2.5.4.description: There is no reliance on device motion, like shaking or tilting, to carry out an action.

2.5.5.title: Target Size (Enhanced)
2.5.5.description: Anything clickable should be at least 44 by 44 pixels, except links within a sentence which are okay to be the size of the text they encompass.

2.5.6.title: Concurrent Input Mechanisms
2.5.6.description: The user can happily switch between using a mouse, touchscreen, keyboard, or any other input device.

2.5.7.title: Dragging Movements
2.5.7.description: An action that is achieved by dragging from one point to another, for example drag-and-drop for reordering, can also be carried out by pressing buttons (‘Move item up', ‘Move item down', etc.). This is related to 2.1.1 Keyboard and 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures.

2.5.8.title: Target Size (Minimum)
2.5.8.description: Anything clickable should be at least 24 by 24 pixels, except links within a sentence which will just be the size of the text.

3.1.1.title: Language of Page
3.1.1.description: There's a lang attribute on the <html> element that matches the language of the page.

3.1.2.title: Language of Parts
3.1.2.description: Any parts of the page that are in a different language to the page itself are marked up with the appropriate lang value. Names and phrases derived from other languages, like “Déjà vu” in English, don't need this.

3.1.3.title: Unusual Words
3.1.3.description: Jargon and figurative language is avoided, or, where not it's possible, the words are defined or clarified the first time they're used on a page.

3.1.4.title: Abbreviations
3.1.4.description: Acronyms and shortened words are avoided; where not that's possible, a definition are provided on each page they're used.

3.1.5.title: Reading Level
3.1.5.description: Writing is kept relatively simple, and is able to be understood by primary school children.

3.1.6.title: Pronunciation
3.1.6.description: If a word can be pronounced more than one way, and each way has a different meaning, the meaning is clarified to avoid ambiguity.

3.2.1.title: On Focus
3.2.1.description: Nothing unexpected changes when something on the page receives keyboard focus, like a <button>

3.2.2.title: On Input
3.2.2.description: Nothing unexpected changes when: the value of a form field, like an <option> in a <select> (dropdown), is chosen.

3.2.3.title: Consistent Navigation
3.2.3.description: Navigation is consistent from page to page.

3.2.4.title: Consistent Identification
3.2.4.description: Things that carry out a particular function should always look and work the same.

3.2.5.title: Change on Request
3.2.5.description: Nothing in the user interfaces changes without the user expressly requesting it using a <button>.

3.2.6.title: Consistent Help
3.2.6.description: Some form of help is available from every page, whether contact details, a contact form, a link to a contact page, or a link to help documentation.

3.3.1.title: Error Identification
3.3.1.description: Error/validation messages should be communicated in text, and should provide suggestions to help the user successfully proceed.

3.3.2.title: Labels or Instructions
3.3.2.description: As much help as is needed is offered to prevent triggering a form error; the form label may be enough, but hint text may also be required.

3.3.3.title: Error Suggestion
3.3.3.description: Error/validation messages should be communicated in text, and should provide suggestions to help the user successfully proceed.

3.3.4.title: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
3.3.4.description: Important forms like a legal agreement or submitting financial information offer the opportunity to check the information entered before sending.

3.3.5.title: Help
3.3.5.description: Where a label can't provide enough information to understand what's being asked, there's hint text or some other kind of explanation alongside.

3.3.6.title: Error Prevention (All)
3.3.6.description: After entering any information, the user is offered the opportunity to check it before sending.

3.3.7.title: Redundant Entry
3.3.7.description:
If the user as already given some information, it's either:
- not asked for again
- pre-populated in the subsequent field
- available to select in a dropdown

3.3.8.title: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
3.3.8.description:
If the user is required to log in, they don't have to remember a password, for example they can:
- copy and paste a password into the right form field
- use password manager software to fill out the log-in details automatically
- have a verification link sent to their emailIt also allows photo recognition, like CAPTCHAs and user-uploaded picture recognition.

3.3.9.title: Accessible Authentication (Enhanced)
3.3.9.description: Almost the same as 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum), but CAPTCHAs and user-uploaded pictures can't be included in the log-in process.

4.1.1.title: Parsing (Obsolete and removed)
4.1.1.description: This has been removed from the specification.

4.1.2.title: Name, Role, Value
4.1.2.description: The semantic meaning of every interactive element (form controls, links, headings, landmarks, tables, and so on) is correct, and each has an accessible name.

4.1.3.title: Status Messages
4.1.3.description: Messages like form errors and success pop-ups are communicated to assistive technology like screen readers.
